newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UBS confirms Ciba floor price of 64/right, 74/shr.
newsitem.headline: UBS confirms Ciba floor price of 64/right, 74/shr.

text.p: Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS), co-lead arranger of Ciba Speciality Chemicals Holding Inc's spin-off from Novartis, confirmed that a bank consortium had fixed a minimum bid price of 64 Swiss francs per Ciba right, representing a 74 franc price per share.

"The global coordinators UBS and CSFB (Credit Suisse First Boston) along with the bank consortium have posted a rights bid floor price of 64 francs, representing 74 francs per share," said John Owen, who is in charge of the transaction for UBS.
Strong retail demand pushed grey market quotes for Ciba shares to around 109 to 111 francs today, dealers said, but the price is likely to fall once rights trading begins tomorrow and volumes swell.
A thin market was keeping prices well above the indicated public offer price of 72 to 86 francs per share announced last week.

The indicative price range values the company being spun off from Novartis at up to 6.21 billion francs. The final issue price and allotment will be announced on March 13 after a complicated system of book-building is completed.
Rights for the shares should be quoted around 10 francs below the expected share price, given the 10 franc exercise price for Novartis shareholders getting them in a one-for-one rights issue.
The consortium will use the rights to get Ciba shares that will be offered to the public in a global issue of at least 300 million francs worth of shares. Share trading starts March 13.
The bank consortium will announce its final rights bid price on the evening of March 10.
